text: Builder.io card in the review strip swaps the sidebar card for one shown while Builder.io isn't connected: Get free AI credits, Run the agent, build full apps, and store files without API keys, and Use Builder.io, over the Builder.io and Agent-Native tiles on an Agent-Native blue and teal wash. The card and its button run the one-click setup and the card goes away once connected

Figma only in the review strip switches the sidebar card and the announcement to a Figma import variant: Import from Figma, whose hero is the Figma upload's header at marketing size, with the same Figma, relay dots and Agent-Native tiles on a still wash where Figma's five colors melt into the Agent-Native blue and teal, light or dark with the theme. Its checklist reads Import Figma files into Agent‑Native Design, Start with the designs you already have, and Continue building as an agentic app, and Import from Figma opens the Figma upload

Sources show their real brand logos in the picker, its header, the Other site builders stack and each import screen: Figma's five colors, Lovable's gradient, Replit orange and Webflow blue, with black marks at full strength that turn white in dark mode. The galaxy keeps white marks on its dark orbs
Removed Paste a URL to import any public website from the announcement's checklist
Tightened the announcement: the line under the title reads Bring a project from another tool into Agent-Native Design, and the last check reads Keep building your project as an agentic app
The announcement's checklist ends with Keep editing, building, and growing your agentic app with Agent-Native Design
The announcement is titled Import an existing project and says what it does: bring a project from another tool into Agent-Native Design and keep building. The sidebar card says the same
The announcement's checklist runs Move a project, then Import a Figma file or a GitHub repository, then Paste a URL, and the sidebar card is titled Import an existing project

The messaging is about turning an imported project into an agentic app built with Agent-Native, whose agent can do anything the UI can: the sidebar card, the announcement, each source's lead, the import steps, and the ready state, which now opens the app
The picker's line under its title reads "Pick where your project lives now, and we'll show you how to import it."
Source headers show three fixed dots that light up in turn from the source to Design, faster while importing. The announcement's logos no longer fall into the mark, and the mark no longer pulses

The announcement moved into a card where Getting started sat in the sidebar, with a small galaxy preview; the card opens the dialog and Import project opens the picker. The galaxy sits in a blue, cyan and teal nebula, and every few seconds a logo falls into the Design mark on a path clear of the others

Dialogs use the toolkit Dialog's corners and close button. Headers pull specks from the source into the Design mark instead of three dots, and the picker's sources drift into it. Every line of copy was rewritten, each tool's steps follow its own help docs, Lovable offers a GitHub route for free plans, and uploads skip .env files and node_modules
The header and announcement gradients use the Agent-Native brand blue and teal, and the announcement's logos orbit at one speed, six per ring, so they never overlap

Added the import workflow. The dashboard opens with an announcement, and Import now opens a picker for Lovable, v0, Bolt, Replit, Base44, Manus, a website, a ZIP, a Figma file, GitHub and other site builders, each with its own steps, then a progress and ready state
